title: Fast advance recovery
rule: Raise when the advance is fully recovered before 80% of the planned work is done (needs the cash inputs).
value_found: month 16 of 24, when only 67% of the work is done
reference_value: CPWD recovers the advance pro rata so that it is fully back when 80% of the work value is done.
reference_source: CPWD GCC cl. 10B(iii) pattern [SEEN]; 80% line [ASSUMPTION, calibrate]
quote: deductions shall be made at the rate of 15% (fifteen percent) of each Stage Payment Statement until such time as the advance payment has been repaid;
explanation: The advance is fully taken back by month 16 of 24, when only 67% of the work is done. After that the bills are cut while the work still needs funding, so the advance helps less than its size suggests. Money at stake: about Rs 10.00 crore (advance taken back from bills before 80% of the work).

title: Performance security high
rule: Raise when performance security is above 5% of value, or an additional security for low bids applies.
value_found: Additional Performance Security if bid is more than 20% below estimate: 20% of the shortfall, capped at 3% of Bid Price
reference_value: Usually 5% of contract value; Dept. of Expenditure order of 12 Nov 2020 cut it to 3%.
reference_source: Manual for Procurement of Works 2022 [SEEN]; DoE OM 12 Nov 2020 [SEEN, via a circular that quotes it]
quote: If the Bid Price offered by the Selected Bidder is lower than 20% of the Estimated Project Cost/ cost put to tender, the Additional Performance Security shall be calculated @20% of the difference
explanation: An extra security applies on top of the normal guarantee: Additional Performance Security if bid is more than 20% below estimate: 20% of the shortfall, capped at 3% of Bid Price. If your bid is well below the estimate you must lock up more bank limit; price this into an aggressive bid. Money at stake: about Rs 3.00 crore (performance security x contract value).

title: No advance, or a costly one
rule: Raise when there is no mobilisation advance, or the advance carries interest, or its guarantee is above 100% of the advance.
value_found: Interest-bearing at Bank Rate + 3% per annum; 110% of the advance
reference_value: Advance should be need-based; interest-free advances are discouraged.
reference_source: Manual for Procurement of Works 2022 [SEEN]; 100% guarantee line [ASSUMPTION]
quote: The Authority shall make an interest-bearing advance payment (the “Advance Payment”) @ “Bank Rate3 + 3%”, equal to 10 % (ten percent) of the Contract Price,
explanation: The advance carries interest (Interest-bearing at Bank Rate + 3% per annum). Compare that rate with your overdraft rate; the advance may cost about the same as borrowing. The advance needs a bank guarantee of 110% of the advance, more than the advance itself. It uses up bank limit and commission for a smaller amount of cash. Money at stake: about Rs 61.67 lakh (interest on the advance, from the cash model).

title: Price variation with holes
rule: Raise when price variation leaves out labour, uses a long index lag, cuts off late-billed work, or applies only above a size or duration this contract does not reach.
value_found: Payable only for stages billed within 30 days of the applicable milestone or Scheduled Completion Date (including extensions)
reference_value: A full price variation covers labour and the main materials, uses recent indices and pays on all work done in the stipulated or extended period.
reference_source: Read from the contract's own clause (C5); lag line [ASSUMPTION]
quote: Price adjustment shall be due and payable only in respect of the stages of Works for which the Stage Payment Statement has been submitted by the Contractor no later than 30 (thirty) days
explanation: Escalation is lost on work not billed in time: Payable only for stages billed within 30 days of the applicable milestone or Scheduled Completion Date (including extensions). A late bill means no price adjustment on that work.

title: Progress-linked termination or heavy withholding
rule: Raise when the employer may terminate on slow progress or once damages hit the cap, or withholds large percentages for missed milestones.
value_found: above that the Contractor is in default and the Authority may terminate
reference_value: Milestone withholding refunded when progress is made good; termination only for real default.
reference_source: Seen in the MP tender (Annexure P) and the MoEF tender (Schedule F) [SEEN]; 1% line [ASSUMPTION]
quote: the total amount of Damages under Clause 10.3 (ii) shall not exceed 10% (ten percent) of the Contract Price
explanation: The employer can end the contract when progress or damages pass a limit (above that the Contractor is in default and the Authority may terminate). On termination you also risk losing your securities, so a bad patch can become a total loss.

title: Deduction rate above the cap
rule: Raise when the retention deduction rate per bill is higher than the stated total cap.
value_found: 6% of each bill with a total cap of 5%; deductions stop after about 83% of the work is billed
reference_value: Not a fault in itself: the higher rate front-loads the deductions until the cap is reached.
reference_source: Seen in the NHAI test agreement (rate 6%, cap 5%) [SEEN]
quote: deduct 6% (six per cent) thereof as guarantee money for performance of the obligations of the Contractor during the Construction Period
explanation: Deductions are 6% of each bill with a total cap of 5%; deductions stop after about 83% of the work is billed. Early bills are cut harder than the cap suggests: use the rate for early-month cash and the cap for the total locked up.

title: Unresolved reference
rule: Raise when an answer points to another document or blank schedule that is not in the package. Targets are normalised (GCC + issuer + year, Schedule X, Annexure X) before grouping.
quote: the lump sum price accepted by the Authority in consideration of the obligations specified in this Agreement for an amount of INR … … … … (INR … … … … … … … …) (the “Contract Price”)
explanation: 1 answer(s) depend on a blank or an unnamed document (cited at Cl. 19.1(i)), which is not in the package (questions 0.3). Get that document, or confirm the terms with the employer.

title: Missing document
rule: Raise ONE flag per package when schedules or conditions are referred to but not supplied.
value_found: Schedule H, Schedule A, Schedule B, Schedule C, Schedule D, Annexure A
quote: Works not exceeding an aggregate value, such value to be determined in accordance with Schedule-H, equal to 10 (ten) percent of the Contract Price. (b) Provided that if any Works cann
explanation: The package refers to 6 document(s) it does not include: Schedule H, Schedule A, Schedule B, Schedule C, Schedule D, Annexure A. Most important for money: Schedule H (sets the stage-payment percentages). Terms in them bind you even though you have not read them; ask the employer for copies.
